e.title: 医疗险费用预测：不只给一个点估计，而是给区间；并主动把一个漂亮数字标注为「只能用来说明机制」
e.title_en: Medical cost prediction: reporting an interval rather than a point estimate, and labelling a flattering number as illustrative of mechanism only
e.title_hk: 醫療險費用預測：不只給一個點估計，而是給區間；並主動把一個漂亮數字標註為「只能用來說明機制」
e.summary: 一个把医疗险费用预测拆成三个问题的单 notebook 项目：哪个模型拟合最好、这个估计到底有多可信、以及模型为何对这个人给出这个数；它用九个回归模型在同一套五折交叉验证下比较、对两个最强候选各做三种调参策略对比、再训练两个 LightGBM 分位数回归器把预测报成最小值／预测值／最大值区间，并用 LIME 给出逐实例解释；它还把一处 0.9925 的 R² 主动标注为「只说明区间机制、不能替代 268 样本的测试指标」
e.summary_hk: 一個把醫療險費用預測拆成三個問題的單 notebook 項目：哪個模型擬合最好、這個估計到底有多可信、以及模型為何對這個人給出這個數；它用九個回歸模型在同一套五折交叉驗證下比較、對兩個最強候選各做三種調參策略對比、再訓練兩個 LightGBM 分位數回歸器把預測報成最小值／預測值／最大值區間，並用 LIME 給出逐實例解釋；它還把一處 0.9925 的 R² 主動標註為「只說明區間機制、不能替代 268 樣本的測試指標」
e.summary_en: A single-notebook project that splits medical insurance cost prediction into three questions: which model fits best, how confident that estimate actually is, and why the model landed on that number for this person; it benchmarks nine regression models under one five-fold cross-validation setup, compares three tuning strategies for each of the two strongest candidates, trains two LightGBM quantile regressors so predictions are reported as a min/prediction/max interval, and adds per-instance LIME explanations — and it labels a flattering R² of 0.9925 as illustrative of the interval mechanism only, not a substitute for the 268-sample test metrics
e.body:
**medical-cost-prediction** 是一个**把医疗险费用预测拆成三个问题的单 notebook 项目**（仓库 `viochris/medical-cost-prediction`），**实测 MIT 许可（根目录实测含 `LICENSE`）、★1、主语言 Jupyter Notebook、仓库体量 2,207 KB、创建于 2026-09-07、最后推送 2026-09-08**（**均 GitHub API 实测值，在解冻窗口内**）；**无 topics**；**README 实测 23,104 字节**。本条目属于本轮主题**「不肯只给一个数」**中的**第四种，也是最字面的一种：它把「一个数」换成了「一个区间」。**

可核实信息（**均 README 与仓库根目录实测**）：**根目录实测只有五项**：**`LICENSE`（1,078 字节）、`README.md`（23,104 字节）、`assets/`、**`medical-cost-prediction.ipynb`（3,404,139 字节）**、`requirements.txt`（1,723 字节）**——**即整个项目是一份 notebook 加其产物**。⭐⭐⭐ **其开篇逐字，是本条目最重要的一段**：**「This repository contains a single, end to end Jupyter notebook (`medical-cost-prediction.ipynb`) that predicts an individual’s medical insurance charges from six demographic and health features. **Rather than stopping at a single "best model" and calling it done, it treats a cost prediction as three separate questions. Which model fits best, how confident should that estimate actually be, and why did the model land on that number for this specific person.**」**；**README 末尾的作者引语逐字为**：**「*"A cost estimate is only as useful as the range and the reasoning behind it."*」**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「把「费用预测」拆成拟合／可信度／这个人为何是这个数三个问题」是本条目的总纲，也是本轮主题最清晰的一次表述**——**逐字见上**；**其流水线逐字为**：**探索性数据分析 → **九个回归模型**在同一套五折交叉验证下的基准比较 → 对两个最强候选做**三种调参策略的三方对比**（`GridSearchCV`／`RandomizedSearchCV`／`Optuna`）→ 最终留出测试集评估 → **基于 LightGBM 的分位数回归给出预测区间而非单点** → **逐实例 LIME 解释**（**并把类别特征映射回可读标签而非编码值**）**。⭐⭐ **对做定价或成本建模的学生，这个三问框架比「我调出一个 R² 0.9」有用得多**——**它把「模型好不好」「这个估计可不可信」「为什么是这个人」分成了三项各自需要交付的东西**。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **「不只给点估计，还给区间」是本条目最直接呼应主题的做法**——**逐字为**：**「Two additional **LightGBM quantile regressors (10th and 90th percentile)** are trained so **every prediction can be reported as a Min, Prediction, and Max range instead of a single dollar figure**.」**；**⚠️ 而它随即**自己指出该区间尚未被检验**——**逐字见下第 ⑤ 条**。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **「在单个模型上与「提前定好赢家」相反的调参设计」是本条目在方法上最值得记的一点**——**其理由逐字为**：**「the two strongest candidates … land close enough to each other, **0.8208 versus 0.8169**, that **picking a single winner from this table alone would have been premature**. **Instead of committing to Random Forest on the spot, both models were carried forward into the hyperparameter tuning stage specifically to check whether tuning might close that small gap, or even flip the ranking entirely**, since it’s entirely possible for a search process to unlock more headroom in one model than the other.」**，**并进一步说明三种调参策略的用意**：**「All three tuning strategies were run for both models **for exactly the reason raised above**, to see whether a more exhaustive search (`GridSearchCV`), a broader but cheaper random sample of the search space (`RandomizedSearchCV`), or a guided, trial-by-trial search (`Optuna`) **would change which model came out ahead, not just to squeeze a few extra points out of a model that had already been decided in advance**.」**⭐⭐⭐ **对做模型选择的学生，这是一条**反直觉但正确**的做法**：**调参的目的**不只是把已选定的模型调得更好**，**更是检验**选择本身是否稳定****；**其结果是 Random Forest 保持领先**（**最终模型参数逐字为 `n_estimators=500, max_depth=27, min_samples_split=6, min_samples_leaf=10, max_features=None, bootstrap=True`**），**但**它逐字承认「**the margin over the best tuned LightGBM result stayed narrow enough that either model would have been a defensible choice**」**——**即**不强称自己的选择是唯一正确的****。**④ ⭐⭐ **其基准结果与解读逐字实测**：**线性族模型（Linear／Ridge／Lasso／Yeo-Johnson 变换后的 Linear）**全部停留在 0.55 至 0.72 之间****，**并给出机制解释**：**「it can’t capture how something like **smoking status doesn’t just add a fixed premium, it multiplies the entire cost curve for that person**」**——⭐⭐ **「吸烟不是加一个固定保费，而是把这个人整条成本曲线乘以一个系数」是**交互项在精算定价中作用**的一个清晰表述****；**最终留出测试集（268 样本）指标逐字为 **R² 0.9014、MAE $2,458.56、RMSE $4,255.67****；**并逐字说明 R² 高于调参期约 0.84 的交叉验证均值是**正常的折间波动****（**「which is a normal amount of movement between a multi-fold average and a single held-out split」**），**以及 RMSE 高于 MAE 是**因为 RMSE 更重罚大偏差，而少数极高费用的病人更难以精确预测****。**⑤ ⭐⭐⭐ **「主动把一个漂亮数字标注为只能说明机制」是本条目最值得引用的一处**——**逐字为**：**「*A quick sanity check on a **10-row subset**, where the point prediction is reported alongside its 10th to 90th percentile quantile interval, **reached an R² of 0.9925**. **That number is only illustrative of the interval mechanism, not a substitute for the 268-sample test metrics above.***」**⭐⭐⭐ **在一个以「R² 越高越好」为默认叙事的领域里，作者**主动把一个 0.9925 的分数降级为机制演示****，**并在斜体附注里写明它**不能替代上面 268 样本的指标****（**可与同轮 [[insurance-fraud-risk-scoring]] 把 PR-AUC 1.00 定性为 bug 报告并读——**两条都在**削弱一个对自己有利的数字****，**但方式不同：一条视其为缺陷线索，一条视其为说明性示例**）。**⑥ ⭐⭐⭐ **「未来工作」中有一条直接质疑自己那个区间**——**逐字为**：**「**Full-set quantile interval evaluation.** Extend the current **10-row** Min, Prediction, and Max demo into a **proper coverage check across the entire 268-row held out set, measuring what fraction of actual charges genuinely fall between the predicted lower and upper bounds**, which is **the real test of whether the interval is trustworthy rather than just illustrative**.」**⭐⭐⭐ **即它明确承认：当前区间**只做了 10 行的演示，尚未做覆盖率检验****，**而**「实际值真正落在上下界之间的比例」才是区间可信与否的真正检验****——**对本轮主题而言，这是最诚实的一处**：**给出区间之后，下一步是检验区间本身准不准**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该项目已完成该覆盖率检验**——**恰好相反，它把此项列为未来工作**）。**⑦ ⭐⭐ **其余未来工作逐字且都属自我批评**：**「Try SHAP alongside LIME」**（**因 SHAP 有一致性理论保证，用以检验两种方法是否在「哪些特征最重要」上一致**，**或是否对同一病人给出明显不同的说法**）；**「Explore stacking or ensembling」**（**逐字说明 `StackingRegressor` **已在 notebook 中 import 但当前未使用****）；**「Collect or source more data」**（**因当前数据集仅 **1,337 条**记录，**用以检验诸如 `region` 近乎零重要度**这类模式是否成立，**或只是该数据集规模的产物**）。⭐⭐ **★「`region` 近乎零重要度可能是样本量造成的假象」这一自我怀疑值得单独记**——**它把**一个看起来像业务发现的结果**主动标为**可能的统计假象****（**⚠️ 本词条**未核实**该判断**——**本次未读其 notebook**）。**⑧ ⭐⭐ **「⚠️ System Limitations」一节逐字含「Architectural Limitations」与「Model & Domain Limitations」两个子节**——**本词条**未读其正文**，**故不转述其具体条目**；**但结论段逐字为**：**「this is still **a single, self-contained analysis rather than a finished, deployable product**, and the two sections below are meant to be read together. **The limitations spell out exactly where the current version falls short, and the future work section spells out what would specifically need to change to close each of those gaps.**」**⭐⭐ **即它把「限制」与「未来工作」明确配成一对**：**前者说当前短在哪里，后者说补哪一步**（**可与第 330 轮 [[claim-to-confidence]] 的「What is real」一节并读——**两者都在**把已完成与未完成分栏****）。**⑨ ⭐ **数据来源与可复现性逐字**：**数据为 Kaggle 的 **Medical Cost Personal Datasets****；**原始 notebook **在 Kaggle 上开发并执行**，**并另在 Kaggle 发布**（**README 给出 Kaggle notebook 链接**）；**最终调优流水线、两个分位数模型与处理后的训练矩阵**均导出为 `.joblib`／`.npy` 以便复用**。**⑩ ⭐ **技术栈逐字**：**scikit-learn 1.3+、LightGBM、Random Forest、Optuna、LIME、pandas、NumPy**；**许可声明逐字为「This project is licensed under the **MIT License**. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.」**（**且 LICENSE 文件实测存在，1,078 字节**——**与第 330／331 轮多例「声称而无文件」形成对照**）；**作者署名逐字为 **Silvio Christian Joe**（@viochris）**。**⑪ ⭐ 可与本站定价与模型选择条目并读**：[[insurance-pricing-tweedie]]、[[easy-glm]]、[[insurance-glm-tools]]、[[insurance-frequency-severity]]、[[shap-relativities]]、[[modelx]]、[[actuarial-benchmarks]]、[[verified-reserving]]、[[reproducible-actuarial-work]]、[[explainable-ai-fraud]]、[[health-insurance-reserving-handbook]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**①** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据、仓库根目录清单（五项）与 README（23,104 字节）全文的开篇三问、流水线概述、关键特征列表、问题陈述、基准与调参两节的解读文字、留出测试与调参期指标数值、10 行子集那段斜体附注、结论段、未来工作四项、许可声明与作者引语**，⭐⭐ **但**未打开、未运行、未读取那份 **`medical-cost-prediction.ipynb`（3,404,139 字节）**、未读 `assets/`、未读 `requirements.txt`、未读 README 中「⚠️ System Limitations」两子节的正文、未复现其任何指标****，因此**不能转述其数据处理细节、九个模型的具体实现、调参搜索空间、分位数模型参数、LIME 输出或其图像**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**其指标数值（R² 0.9014、MAE $2,458.56、RMSE $4,255.67、基准 0.8208／0.8169、线性族 0.55–0.72、10 行子集 0.9925）的真实性与可复现性**——**本次完全未运行其 notebook**；**本词条只记录其**自述的数值与解读**，**不主张**任何数值正确**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**其**分位数区间**的实际覆盖率**——**README 自己把「全量覆盖率检验」列为未来工作**，**即**本词条**不主张**该区间目前可信**；**这是本条目最需要后续核实的一处**；**④ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其「⚠️ System Limitations」两子节的具体条目**（**本次未读其正文**）；**⑤ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其 9 个模型基准与三种调参策略对比的实际运行情况**；**⑥ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其 LIME 解释与（未做的）SHAP 对照**，**亦未核实**其将类别特征映射回可读标签的实现**；**⑦ ⭐ ⚠️ **该数据集仅 **1,337 条**记录，且为美国某保险数据集的公开样本****——**作者本人已指出小样本可能造成「`region` 近乎零重要度」这类**统计假象****；**本词条据此**不主张**其模型、系数或特征重要度可外推到任何真实的医疗保险组合或费率制定**；**⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ **医疗费用预测涉及**健康相关属性**（年龄、BMI、吸烟状况等）**——**此类变量在保险定价中常受**监管限制或禁止使用****；**本词条**不主张**该模型的特征选择在任何辖区可用于真实定价**（**本次未评估其合规性**）；**⑨ ⭐ ⚠️ **该项目自述为**「一份自成一体的分析，而非完成的可部署产品」****；**本词条**不主张**其可用于任何真实的定价、核保、预算或监管用途**；**⑩ ⭐ ★1、fork 0**，**关注度极低**（**★1**），**不主张其成熟度、方法优越性或已被采用**；**⑪ ⭐ **根目录实测无 `tests/`、无 CI 配置****——**与同轮含 CI 徽章与测试套件的条目不同**；**本词条仅记录这一结构差异，不作价值判断**；**⑫ ⭐ 无 topics**；**⑬ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**（**README 实测为英文**）。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/viochris/medical-cost-prediction`、`/readme` 与 `/contents/` 于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取（README 23,104 字节经 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 实测逐字核对，含开篇三问、流水线、基准与调参解读、留出测试指标、10 行子集斜体附注、结论段、未来工作四项、许可声明与作者引语）；**未打开该 3.4 MB 的 notebook、未运行任何代码、未复核任何数值**。

**medical-cost-prediction** is **a single-notebook project that splits medical insurance cost prediction into three questions** (repository `viochris/medical-cost-prediction`), with **measured MIT licence (a `LICENSE` file is present at the root), ★1, Jupyter Notebook as the primary language, a 2,207 KB repository, created 2026-09-07 and last pushed 2026-09-08** (**all GitHub API measurements, inside the thaw window**); it has **no topics**; **the README measures 23,104 bytes**. It is the fourth of this round’s four takes on **refusing to give just one number**, **and the most literal: it replaces a single number with an interval**.

Verifiable details (**all measured from the README and the repository root**): **the root measurably contains exactly five items**: **`LICENSE` (1,078 bytes), `README.md` (23,104 bytes), `assets/`, `medical-cost-prediction.ipynb` (3,404,139 bytes) and `requirements.txt` (1,723 bytes)** — **the project is one notebook plus its artefacts**. ⭐⭐⭐ **Its opening, read verbatim, is the entry’s most important passage**: **"This repository contains a single, end to end Jupyter notebook (`medical-cost-prediction.ipynb`) that predicts an individual’s medical insurance charges from six demographic and health features. Rather than stopping at a single \"best model\" and calling it done, it treats a cost prediction as three separate questions. Which model fits best, how confident should that estimate actually be, and why did the model land on that number for this specific person."**; **and the author’s closing line reads verbatim**: **"*\"A cost estimate is only as useful as the range and the reasoning behind it.\"*"**

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ Splitting cost prediction into three questions — fit, confidence, and why this person got this number — is the entry’s organising idea and the clearest statement of this round’s theme** — **its pipeline reads verbatim as**: **exploratory data analysis → a nine-model regression benchmark under one five-fold cross-validation setup → a three-way hyperparameter tuning comparison (`GridSearchCV` vs `RandomizedSearchCV` vs `Optuna`) for the two strongest candidates → final held-out test evaluation → LightGBM-based quantile regression to produce a prediction interval instead of a point → per-instance LIME explanation** (**with categorical features mapped back to human-readable labels rather than encoded numbers**). ⭐⭐ **For students of pricing or cost modelling, that three-question frame is far more useful than "I tuned a model to R² 0.9" — it splits delivery into three separate things: whether the model is good, how much the estimate can be trusted, and why it is this number for this person.** **② ⭐⭐⭐ Reporting an interval rather than a point estimate is the entry’s most direct response to this round’s theme** — verbatim: **"Two additional LightGBM quantile regressors (10th and 90th percentile) are trained so every prediction can be reported as a Min, Prediction, and Max range instead of a single dollar figure."**; **⚠️ and it immediately notes that the interval has not been tested — see item ⑤ below**. **③ ⭐⭐⭐ Refusing to pick a winner in advance is the entry’s most notable methodological point** — its reasoning reads verbatim: **"the two strongest candidates … land close enough to each other, 0.8208 versus 0.8169, that picking a single winner from this table alone would have been premature. Instead of committing to Random Forest on the spot, both models were carried forward into the hyperparameter tuning stage specifically to check whether tuning might close that small gap, or even flip the ranking entirely, since it’s entirely possible for a search process to unlock more headroom in one model than the other."**, **with the purpose of the three tuning strategies stated further**: **"All three tuning strategies were run for both models for exactly the reason raised above, to see whether a more exhaustive search (`GridSearchCV`), a broader but cheaper random sample of the search space (`RandomizedSearchCV`), or a guided, trial-by-trial search (`Optuna`) would change which model came out ahead, not just to squeeze a few extra points out of a model that had already been decided in advance."** ⭐⭐⭐ **For students of model selection this is a counter-intuitive but correct practice: tuning is not only about improving an already-chosen model, but about testing whether the choice itself is stable**; **the outcome was that Random Forest kept the lead** (**final parameters verbatim `n_estimators=500, max_depth=27, min_samples_split=6, min_samples_leaf=10, max_features=None, bootstrap=True`**), **but it states verbatim that "the margin over the best tuned LightGBM result stayed narrow enough that either model would have been a defensible choice" — it does not claim its own choice was the only right one**. **④ ⭐⭐ Its baseline results and their reading read verbatim**: **the linear-family models all plateau between 0.55 and 0.72**, **with a mechanistic explanation**: **"it can’t capture how something like smoking status doesn’t just add a fixed premium, it multiplies the entire cost curve for that person"** — ⭐⭐ **a clear statement of what an interaction term does in actuarial pricing**; **the held-out test metrics (268 samples) read verbatim as R² 0.9014, MAE $2,458.56 and RMSE $4,255.67**; **and it explains verbatim that an R² above the roughly 0.84 cross-validation average from tuning is "a normal amount of movement between a multi-fold average and a single held-out split", and that RMSE exceeding MAE is expected because RMSE penalises large misses more heavily and a handful of very high-cost patients are harder to predict**. **⑤ ⭐⭐⭐ Voluntarily labelling a flattering number as illustrative of mechanism only is the entry’s most quotable passage** — verbatim: **"*A quick sanity check on a 10-row subset, where the point prediction is reported alongside its 10th to 90th percentile quantile interval, reached an R² of 0.9925. That number is only illustrative of the interval mechanism, not a substitute for the 268-sample test metrics above.*"** ⭐⭐⭐ **In a field whose default narrative is "higher R² is better", the author voluntarily downgrades a 0.9925 to a mechanism demonstration and states in italics that it cannot substitute for the 268-sample metrics above** (**readable with this round’s [[insurance-fraud-risk-scoring]], which calls a PR-AUC of 1.00 a bug report — both weaken a number that favours them, but one treats it as a defect signal and the other as an illustrative example**). **⑥ ⭐⭐⭐ One future-work item directly questions its own interval** — verbatim: **"Full-set quantile interval evaluation. Extend the current 10-row Min, Prediction, and Max demo into a proper coverage check across the entire 268-row held out set, measuring what fraction of actual charges genuinely fall between the predicted lower and upper bounds, which is the real test of whether the interval is trustworthy rather than just illustrative."** ⭐⭐⭐ **It openly admits that the interval is so far a 10-row demonstration without a coverage check, and that the fraction of actual values genuinely falling between the bounds is the real test of trustworthiness — for this round’s theme, the most honest passage: having produced an interval, the next step is to test the interval itself** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim that coverage check has been done — on the contrary, the README lists it as future work**). **⑦ ⭐⭐ The remaining future-work items read verbatim and are all self-critical**: **"Try SHAP alongside LIME"** (**because SHAP offers stronger theoretical consistency guarantees, to see whether the two methods agree on which features matter, or tell noticeably different stories for the same patient**); **"Explore stacking or ensembling"** (**noting verbatim that `StackingRegressor` is already imported in the notebook but currently unused**); and **"Collect or source more data"** (**because the dataset is limited to 1,337 records, to test whether patterns like the near-zero importance of `region` hold up or are an artefact of this dataset’s size**). ⭐⭐ **That self-doubt about `region` deserves separate note: a result that looks like a business finding is voluntarily flagged as a possible statistical artefact** (**⚠️ the entry did not verify that judgement — the notebook was not read**). **⑧ ⭐⭐ A "⚠️ System Limitations" section measurably contains "Architectural Limitations" and "Model & Domain Limitations" subsections** — **their bodies were not read**, **so their specific items are not restated**; **but the conclusion reads verbatim**: **"this is still a single, self-contained analysis rather than a finished, deployable product, and the two sections below are meant to be read together. The limitations spell out exactly where the current version falls short, and the future work section spells out what would specifically need to change to close each of those gaps."** ⭐⭐ **Limitations and future work are explicitly paired** (**readable with round 330’s [[claim-to-confidence]] and its "What is real" section — both separate what is done from what is not**). **⑨ ⭐ Data provenance and reproducibility read verbatim**: **the data is Kaggle’s Medical Cost Personal Datasets**; **the original notebook was developed and executed on Kaggle and is also published there** (**the README links to the Kaggle notebook**); and **the final tuned pipeline, the two quantile models and the processed training matrix are exported as `.joblib` / `.npy` for reuse**. **⑩ ⭐ Its stack reads verbatim**: **scikit-learn 1.3+, LightGBM, Random Forest, Optuna, LIME, pandas, NumPy**; **the licence statement reads verbatim "This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details."** (**and the `LICENSE` file measurably exists at 1,078 bytes — contrasting with the several "claim without a file" cases in rounds 330 and 331**); **and the author is credited verbatim as Silvio Christian Joe (@viochris)**. **⑪ ⭐ Readable with the site’s pricing and model-selection entries**: [[insurance-pricing-tweedie]], [[easy-glm]], [[insurance-glm-tools]], [[insurance-frequency-severity]], [[shap-relativities]], [[modelx]], [[actuarial-benchmarks]], [[verified-reserving]], [[reproducible-actuarial-work]], [[explainable-ai-fraud]] and [[health-insurance-reserving-handbook]].

**the entry records only the author’s stated figures and readings, and claims none of them correct**; **③ ⭐⭐⭐ The actual coverage of its quantile interval was not verified** — **the README itself lists a full-set coverage check as future work**, **so the entry does not claim the interval is currently trustworthy**; **this is the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**; **④ ⭐⭐ The specific items of its two "⚠️ System Limitations" subsections were not verified** (**their bodies were not read**); **⑦ ⭐ ⚠️ The dataset has only 1,337 records and is a public sample of a US insurance dataset** — **the author himself notes that a small sample may cause statistical artefacts such as the near-zero importance of `region`**;
